outcome_intro: Google gives MSPs no cross-client admin console: every client is its own Admin console login. Register each client once (a service account with domain-wide delegation), then ask your AI "who still has no 2-Step Verification across all my clients," "which paid licenses can I reclaim," or "were last month's leavers fully offboarded," and get one ranked answer across every tenant, read live and in parallel.

instead_of_say.instead: Logging into each client's Admin console, filtering Users by 2-Step Verification enrollment, and copying the unenrolled admins into a spreadsheet, one client at a time
instead_of_say.say: Which accounts across all my clients still don't have 2-Step Verification, admins first?

instead_of_say.instead: Exporting each client's users and license assignments and matching suspended, never-signed-in, and idle accounts that still hold a paid seat
instead_of_say.say: Which paid Google Workspace licenses can I reclaim across my clients?

instead_of_say.instead: Working through the offboarding checklist by hand in the Admin console, where suspending the account too early blocks the backup-code cleanup that has to run first
instead_of_say.say: Preview offboarding jane@example.com and hand her Drive and Calendar to her manager

pain_points: On r/msp's "Google Workspace Management" thread (June 2026) the original poster asked for "a CIPP equivalent for the GW side"; another MSP managing about 10 Workspace tenants out of roughly 250 clients called it "a manual process for the most part." Microsoft has GDAP and CIPP; Google has no cross-client admin view, so every client is a separate Admin console login.

The common workaround is GAM: "multi tenant GAM ... you just GAM select company to switch companies," as one reply in the same thread put it. GAM can loop a command over every client section, but each fleet question still means writing that loop and query yourself, and anything that joins users with licenses, admin roles, or audit events is a script you maintain.

Google bills a suspended account the same as an active one (Google Workspace Admin Help, "Preserve data for users who leave your organization"), so every leaver who was suspended instead of moved to an Archived User license, or never cleaned up at all, keeps costing the client a paid seat until someone finds it.

outcomes.question: Which accounts across all my clients lack 2-Step Verification, with unenrolled admins first?
Which Google Workspace licenses sit on suspended, never-signed-in, or idle accounts, per client?
Did our suspended leavers keep a license, groups, an admin role, OAuth tokens, or an unfinished Drive transfer?
Where does each client stand on 2SV coverage, admins without 2SV, stale licenses, and Drive and Calendar setting changes?
Who changed Drive or Calendar settings, and which files went external or public, in the last week?
Which third-party apps hold full mail, full Drive, or admin access to client data?
Any suspicious sign-ins, hijacked accounts, or 2SV turned off across clients this week?
What would offboarding this leaver do, step by step, before anything changes?
Is every client's domain-wide delegation still authorized, scope by scope?

different_vs_wrappers: Most Google Workspace MCP servers, such as [taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp](https://github.com/taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp), work inside one organization's Gmail, Drive, and Docs. [GAM](https://github.com/GAM-team/GAM) keeps one config section per client and can loop a command over every section into one CSV, but you write the loop, the query, and any join across users, licenses, admin roles, and audit logs yourself. This skill keeps a registry of client tenants, each with its own service account and least-privilege scope profile, and fans one question out across all of them in parallel: 2SV gaps, license waste, incomplete offboarding, sharing drift, risky OAuth apps, and sign-in alerts come back as one ranked table, with any tenant it could not read listed as a failure rather than silently dropped.
different_vs_vendor: The Google Admin console stays the place for deep single-client work and for settings the API does not expose. This skill adds what the console does not have: one view across every client domain you manage, driven from whichever AI agent you already use, plus an offboarding runbook that previews every step with live reads and suspends the account last, after the backup-code invalidation that fails on a suspended account.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS. google-workspace-mcp speaks HTTP natively: run it with `--transport http` and a `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN`, then put its /mcp endpoint behind an HTTPS tunnel or your own reverse proxy. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You register each client once with `tenants add`.

faqs.q: Is my Google Workspace data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. Each client's service-account key is copied into the CLI's config directory with owner-only permissions (mode 0600 on macOS and Linux; on Windows the file inherits the config folder's permissions), and tokens are minted on demand and sent only to Google. Credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.

faqs.q: How do I connect a client's Google Workspace?
faqs.a: In a Google Cloud project, create a service account and download its JSON key, and enable the Admin SDK API and the Enterprise License Manager API (plus the Cloud Identity API for the `policy` profile). Run `google-workspace-cli tenants add <name> --domain <client domain> --admin <client super admin> --key <key file>`. It prints the Client ID and the scopes to paste into the client's Admin console under Security, Access and data control, API controls, Domain-wide delegation. Then `google-workspace-cli tenants test <name>` confirms Google issues a token for every delegated scope.

faqs.q: Does an agent get write access to my clients?
faqs.a: Only what you authorize per client. The default `read` scope profile covers the reports, but Google has no read-only scope for OAuth tokens or app passwords, and none for license assignments, so that profile can still revoke tokens, sign users out, read backup codes, turn off 2SV, and change licenses: keep those commands human-in-the-loop. Offboarding writes need the `full` profile, and `offboard` only previews unless you pass `--yes` on the command line, which an MCP client cannot do. Setting `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_MCP_READ_ONLY` to exactly `1` also hides the MCP server's write tools.

faqs.q: Will this hit Google's API quotas?
faqs.a: The cross-client commands query Google live, so they count against the Admin SDK quota of the Google Cloud project that owns each client's service account. `--concurrency` caps how many clients run in parallel, `--max-scan-pages` caps paging, and a client whose calls fail or hit the page cap is listed in `fetch_failures` rather than silently dropped.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

governance_summary: Each client is a registered tenant whose service account impersonates that client's super admin with only the scopes you grant. The cross-client reports (mfa-gaps, stale-licenses, leavers, posture, sharing-drift, oauth-apps, login-alerts) only read. The default read scope profile still allows token revocation, sign-out, backup-code reads, 2SV turn-off, and license changes, because Google offers no read-only scope for those surfaces, so those commands are human-in-the-loop. Offboarding needs the full profile and only acts with an explicit --yes.
